title: Involtini di Manzo
subtitle: Italian beef rolls stuffed with breadcrumbs, parsley and parmesan
excerpt: Involtini di manzo are thin slices of beef rolled around a filling of breadcrumbs, garlic, parsley, and parmesan, then braised slowly in tomato sauce. They are a Sunday dish across southern Italy, where the braising sauce is then used to dress pasta. The beef becomes very tender during the long braise and the filling seasons the sauce from the inside.
sourceNotes: Involtini di manzo is a classic of southern Italian Sunday cooking. In Sicily and Calabria the rolls are called braciole and the braising sauce is served over pasta as a first course. The dish is a classic of cucina povera -- thin, inexpensive cuts of beef made flavoursome by slow braising in tomato sauce.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the involtini in their sauce. Reheat gently.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Improves the next day. The braising sauce can be used to dress pasta.

content.text: Ask the butcher for thin slices of beef topside or silverside, beaten out to about 3 to 4 mm. The slices need to be thin enough to roll without tearing, and large enough to hold a tablespoon of filling. Secure each roll with kitchen string or a cocktail stick before browning -- the filling must stay inside during the braise.

items.prepNote: in 8 thin slices about 3mm thick, beaten flat

content.text: Put {{breadcrumbs-dried}} breadcrumbs, {{parmesan}} Parmesan, {{parsley-flat}} parsley, and grated {{garlic}} garlic into a bowl. Add {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil, {{salt-table}} salt, and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Mix to a firm paste.
Lay out {{beef-rump}} beef slices. Divide the filling between them, spreading it evenly and leaving a 1 cm border. Roll each slice tightly and secure with kitchen string or a cocktail stick.

Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Brown the rolls on all sides, about 4 minutes total. Remove. Reduce heat to medium, add {{onion}} onion to the pan, and cook for 5 minutes. Add chopped {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute. Pour in {{red-wine}} wine and simmer for 2 minutes.

Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes and season with {{salt-table}} salt. Return the rolls to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 60 to 75 minutes, turning the rolls once, until the beef is very tender. Remove the string or sticks before serving. Serve the sauce over pasta as a first course, then the rolls as the main.

items.cause: The string or sticks worked loose.
items.fix: Use two pieces of string per roll, one at each end, to hold the filling securely. Cocktail sticks alone often work loose in long braises -- use string instead.

content.text: Involtini appear across southern Italy and Sicily under different names. In Sicily they are called braciole al sugo; in Calabria, lu ruotulu. The central idea -- thin beef rolled around a filling, braised in tomato sauce -- is the same everywhere. In the traditional Sunday meal structure, the braising sauce serves as the pasta course (il primo), and the involtini are the meat course (il secondo). This is the model of southern Italian Sunday cooking: one pot, two courses.
